qa.question: Should the three Paradise gas turbines be 231.2 MW instead of 250 MW?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives 231.2 MW nameplate for each of the three simple cycle turbines CT5, CT6 and CT7. GEM shows 250 MW each, which matches the TVA environmental review figure. The Kentucky air permit record lists 229 MW at 59 degrees for these turbines.
qa.recommendation: Check the Tennessee Valley Authority nameplate or the generator data sheet. If it confirms 231.2 MW, change units 4, 5 and 6 to 231.2 MW.
qa.note: The Kentucky draft Title V air permit V-26-011 (https://dep.gateway.ky.gov/eSearch.WebApi/api/documentGenerate/getDocument/14331535) rates each of these turbines at 229 MW at 59 degrees Fahrenheit and the Tennessee Valley Authority plant page (https://www.tva.com/energy/our-power-system/natural-gas/paradise-combined-cycle-plant) says three turbines add 681 MW, which is 227 MW each. The 250 MW figure in GEM matches the environmental review. The combined cycle block matches the EIA total of 1,160 MW.
